dimensions.assessment: Federal agencies (DOJ, FTC, SBA) and small businesses filing antitrust complaints are affected by the reporting mandate.
dimensions.evidence: the head of each specified entity shall submit to the Chief Counsel for Advocacy of the Office of Advocacy of the Small Business Administration a report

dimensions.assessment: Establishes administrative reporting and review processes without altering underlying antitrust enforcement powers or small business operations directly.
dimensions.evidence: requires the Department of Justice (DOJ) and the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) to separately report biennially to the Small Business Administration (SBA)

dimensions.assessment: Involves administrative duties within existing agencies with no direct spending appropriations or revenue changes specified.
dimensions.evidence: The Chief Counsel for Advocacy shall submit to the Committee on Small Business of the House... a report that includes...

dimensions.assessment: Amends the Small Business Economic Policy Act of 1980 to replace an annual presidential report requirement with agency reporting rules.
dimensions.evidence: The bill replaces a requirement that the President report annually to Congress about the role of small businesses in the economy on an industry-by-industry basis.

dimensions.assessment: Establishes an ongoing biennial reporting cycle for federal agencies.
dimensions.evidence: Not later than 180 days after the end of the fiscal year... and every two fiscal years thereafter

missing_information: Cost to federal agencies of compiling and reviewing the new reports is not estimated.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill modifies federal reporting requirements for the Department of Justice, the Federal Trade Commission, and the Small Business Administration regarding antitrust enforcement and small businesses.
